verses.text: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? Are you not the result of my work in the Lord?
Others may not think of me as an apostle, but surely you do. You yourselves are the proof that I am the Lord's apostle.
This is my answer to those who question me.
Do we not have the right to food and drink?
Do we not have the right to take a believing wife with us, as the other apostles do, and the Lord's brothers, and Cephas?
Or are Barnabas and I the only ones who must work for a living?
What soldier pays his own costs? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat its grapes? Who looks after a flock and does not drink its milk?
Is this just human thinking? Does the law not say the same thing?
For it is written in the law of Moses, "Do not tie up the mouth of an ox while it is treading out the grain." Is it oxen that God is worried about?
Is he not really speaking for our sake? Yes, this was written for us. The one who ploughs and the one who threshes should both work in the hope of sharing in the harvest.
We planted spiritual seed among you. Is it too much to ask for a harvest of material help from you?
If others have this right, surely we have it even more. But we did not use this right. We put up with anything rather than get in the way of the good news about Christ.
Do you not know that those who work in the temple get their food from the temple? Those who serve at the altar share in what is offered on the altar.
In the same way, the Lord has commanded that those who preach the good news should get their living from the good news.
But I have not used any of these rights. And I am not writing this so that you will do these things for me. I would rather die than let anyone take away my reason to boast.
Preaching the good news gives me no reason to boast, because I must do it. How terrible it would be for me if I did not preach the good news!
If I did it because I chose to, I would have a reward. But I do not do it by my own choice. I have been trusted with this work.
So what is my reward? It is this: that I can preach the good news free of charge, and not use my right to be paid for it.
I am free and belong to no one. But I have made myself a slave to everyone, to win as many people as possible.
With Jews, I became like a Jew, to win Jews. With those under the law, I became like someone under the law, though I myself am not under the law, to win those under the law.
With those who do not have the law, I became like someone without the law, to win them. This does not mean I am free from God's law. I am under Christ's law.
With the weak, I became weak, to win the weak. I have become all things to all people, so that by every possible way I might save some.
I do all this for the sake of the good news, so that I can share in its blessings.
Do you not know that in a race all the runners run, but only one gets the prize? So run in a way that will win the prize.
Everyone who competes in the games trains hard and controls themselves. They do it to win a crown that will not last. But we do it to win a crown that will last for ever.
So I do not run without a goal. I do not fight like a boxer hitting the air.
No, I train my body hard and make it obey me. Then, after I have preached to others, I myself will not be disqualified.
